title: From a port list to a homelab in Docker

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ever set up a server and forget which app lives on port eight-oh-nine-six?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Constantly. I've got sticky notes with port numbers on them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine had the same problem. He kept a private list of self-hosted apps to try, mostly to stop handing out random ports. That list grew into MediaBoxDockerCompose on GitHub.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One Docker Compose file, shared paths on disk, and a lot of lessons from trying things at home. The idea is one host, many containers, shared volumes. Jellyfin sits next to a torrent client and an RSS reader, without a new virtual machine for each hobby.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What did he actually wire up?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jellyfin for playback, Airsonic for music, Piwigo for family photos. For operations there's Netdata for disk and load at a glance, and Guacamole for remote desktops in a browser. For notes there's BookStack, FreshRSS and Gitea, and draw.io for diagrams.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And a trick on the ports?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He plans them in families, mostly the eight-thousand range. That kept his firewall rules and his reverse proxy simple.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What if Compose isn't the right shape?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then he uses Proxmox helper scripts. They're community one-liners: paste one into the Proxmox shell, choose default or advanced, and you get a container plus an update menu. Compose suits shared volumes. Separate containers suit hard isolation.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Like choosing between an open-plan office and separate rooms.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. He's run both on the same rack. And the original wish list had eighty-six Docker names; the repo README holds the ports and install steps.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Where does a listener go next?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The full write-up has the photo of the wall stack and the service tables, and the README acts as the manual.
